status: Reviewed shorter context groups; publication requested; source readings unchanged.
scope: Supplied source through Chapter1 closing59; original uncertain readings remain unresolved.
basis: Manual review of the existing Kannada-script Sanskrit and matching Kannada paragraphs; original Devanagari archive available as secondary script reference. No new OCR, source text or conjectural completion.
editorial_limit: Context boundaries are proposed reading divisions, not traditional textual divisions or completed guru approval.
invocation: Separate invocation remains unchanged before numbered groups.

groups.topic: Meditation on Ganesa and his nature
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse1 meditates on Ganesa;2 describes his cosmic scope,3 his manifestations for devotees, and4 closes this Ganesa-focused passage with salutation and the human/elephant distinction. Begin the wider invocations at5.

groups.topic: Wider salutations and the purpose of invocation
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep the salutations to the other named divine forms and sages together. Verse7 explicitly closes with seeking their refuge for knowledge of the Puranas; the narrative setting starts at8.

groups.topic: Why the sages assembled in Naimisaranya
groups.boundary_rationale: The sages fear Kali, choose the forest, pursue their duties, and undertake Purana hearing. Verse10 finishes the stated motivation before Suta arrives at11. Its uncertain final cluster is retained, not reconstructed.

groups.topic: Suta arrives and beholds the forest
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse11 introduces the arriving visitor and12 his response to the forest. The focus shifts from the forest to the assembled sages at13.

groups.topic: Portrait of the assembled sages
groups.boundary_rationale: These connected descriptions cover the sages daily duties, Vedic study, radiance and role as guides. Verse16 returns to Suta action, so the portrait ends at15.

groups.topic: Salutation before Suta speaks
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep the arrival, prostration, greetings and joined hands together, including the narrative announcement that he is about to speak. The explicit Suta speech begins at18.

groups.topic: Suta complete greeting of gratitude
groups.boundary_rationale: The explicit Suta speech at18 continues through praise of the sages and their feet, and culminates in his repeated declaration of fulfilment and liberation at21. Do not cut this speech after18 or20. Verse21 stays reunited across PDF14 and15.

groups.topic: The sages reply to Suta
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse22 introduces the reply and23 contains the Brahmanas actual invitation and satisfaction. Keeping the lead-in with its reply avoids leaving an announcement detached from the words it introduces.

groups.topic: Seating and transition to the next inquiry
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep the narrative seating and attention of the assembled sages together before the explicit Shaunaka speech at26. The reading and meaning in25 remain provisional; this boundary does not infer the uncertain names or repair their wording.

groups.topic: Shaunaka identifies Suta authority through Vyasa
groups.boundary_rationale: Shaunaka addresses Suta, refers to his teacher, describes that teachers work, and links it to Suta knowledge. The reason for the present gathering resumes at29.

groups.topic: Need for the gathering and the request to hear a Purana
groups.boundary_rationale: The speakers fear of Kali, Suta timely presence and the request for Purana narration form one connected appeal. Verse31 completes the request;32 begins a further direct commendation.

groups.topic: Removal of doubts and the name Romaharsana
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse32 praises the visitor as a remover of doubts and33 continues that thought in explaining his name. Keep the explanation with its premise; the narrative introduces Suta response at34. The unclear ending in32 stays unresolved.

groups.topic: Suta response and promise
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse34 announces Suta delighted response;35 gives his actual promise to recount what Vyasa taught. The act of recounting and description of that material begins at36.

groups.topic: The Puranas being narrated and their qualities
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep the narration and its connected description of narratives, teachings, benefits and the Purana/Upapurana/Itihasa material together. Verse39 changes focus to the listeners reaction. The existing meaning-gap flag38 remains flagged.

groups.topic: The sages reception of the narration
groups.boundary_rationale: Verse39 describes repeated hearing and the sages delight;40 continues the narrative about the sages and passage of time. Keep this connection without claiming an exact duration or completing the unclear wording in40. The new difficulty is introduced at41.

groups.topic: The difficulty that prompts a new question
groups.boundary_rationale: Different teachings leave the sages unable to reach a conclusion;42 explicitly introduces Shaunaka next inquiry. This narrative problem statement ends before his quoted question at43.

groups.topic: Shaunaka question and transition to Suta answer
groups.boundary_rationale: Separate the framing question43–44 from the examples and full request45–48 plus answer transition49; dependent list46–47 remains together.
groups.readability_revision: Natural subtopic split; scripture and individual meanings unchanged.

groups.topic: Shaunaka question and transition to Suta answer
groups.boundary_rationale: Separate the framing question43–44 from the examples and full request45–48 plus answer transition49; dependent list46–47 remains together.
groups.readability_revision: Natural subtopic split; scripture and individual meanings unchanged.

groups.topic: Destruction of the sacrifice and Daksha plight
groups.boundary_rationale: Suta introduces the recalled event, destruction and restoration, ending with Daksha unsettled state. Mudgala arrives at55.

groups.topic: Mudgala arrival and reception
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep Mudgala arrival and description with Daksha reception, ending before the explicit request at58.

groups.topic: Daksha appeal and Mudgala reply
groups.boundary_rationale: Keep the short request for help together with the response to remember Vighnaraja; the source chapter colophon follows59.
